item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Well Gears, congratulations on writing the first piece of fiction to make me feel physically, non-hyperbolically sick. Perhaps it was because I read this shortly after having breakfast, perhaps it was because I was reading this while in a moving vehicle, the fact remains that you were able to make your descriptions of these grotesque things being done to these poor people so grounded and relatable in spite of their otherworldliness to such a degree that I actually felt ill for a bit. Even fifteen minutes after having stopped 3/4th of the way through and actively attempting to breathe as regularly as possible to calm my stomach down I was still a bit lightheaded.

And the great thing is that in most cases this effect would be cause for me to dislike what I read because it implies a reliance on cheap grossout value rather than true horror, but that wasn't the case here - even if all of those descriptions were cut out the story would still hold up - the grotesqueries improve the story rather than prop up something that'd be insubstantial without them.

Kudos to you!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
…..I have never had nightmares about things I've read or watched. I've had certain scenes I've seen replay in my head before, but generally me going to sleep is an easy task, and any nightmares I have are of my mind's own invention.

I'm laying in bed right now, typing on my phone. I was working on falling asleep when a single line entered my head: he didn't know it, but he had run for four days before 106 began taking chunks out of him. I then found myself vividly imagining the torso scene and the guy running in terror. I then started thinking about real life scenarios with 106. How could one escape him. How far can he travel through the pocket dimension, and how quickly. If someone were on a boat in the ocean, or on a plane in the sky, would they be safe until they reached solid ground? If they're on the other side of the world, does he know where they are and it's just a matter of time till he gets them?

And then I wondered how much he values the hunt, the chase. Would he take someone in their sleep? Or simply wait in their room until they woke up? And then I began imagining him in here with me. And now I'm having trouble falling asleep, for the first time EVER, from something I read. And for once I am worried that, once asleep, I may dream of him.

You're doing the devil's work here, Gears. Keep it up.

That all said…..I've noticed you've been focusing on 106 a lot lately. There is no question, he is awesome, but I suggest branching out a bit into your other material more. Know what I want to see? A SCP-455 tale. You have said before that that is a true horror…..show us why :). SCP-238 too, I've always wanted to know more about that one….
